title: Failure-driven repair of a scientific optimization strategy
objective: Develop and stress-test a compact optimization strategy for a family containing smooth, ill-conditioned, multimodal, and noisy objectives under bounded evaluation budgets. Begin with a defensible baseline, identify where and why it fails, introduce only evidence-motivated changes, and determine whether the repaired strategy improves robustness without hiding cost in extra evaluations or privileged initialization.
success_definition: The result must include genuine failure cases, a causally motivated repair, equal-budget comparisons over multiple seeds, and an honest account of regimes where the repair does not help.
deliverables: A frozen objective-family and initialization protocol.
Baseline failure evidence across multiple seeds.
At least one repair motivated by an observed failure mechanism.
Equal-evaluation-budget comparison with uncertainty and reproducible code.
resources: Optional warpbubble optimization package, resolved through ASTRA_WARPBUBBLE_OPT_ROOT
linear_control_directions: Define smooth, ill-conditioned, multimodal, and noisy objective functions.
Run a local gradient-based baseline under a fixed evaluation budget.
Run a derivative-free baseline under the same budget.
Measure sensitivity to initialization over frozen seeds.
Add a multistart strategy to the stronger baseline.
Add a simple noise-robust acceptance or averaging rule.
Compare all strategies at equal objective-evaluation counts.
Summarize robust gains, failure regimes, and computational cost.

expert_anchors.goal_advancement: How convincingly the work develops a more robust strategy from observed failures under equal budgets.
expert_anchors.hypothesis_quality: Specificity and testability of proposed failure mechanisms and repairs.
expert_anchors.research_depth: Whether the investigation forms a failure-observation-repair-retest chain rather than a flat algorithm comparison.
expert_anchors.evidence_quality: Fair evaluation counts, seeds, uncertainty, reachable failures, and avoidance of initialization or tuning leakage.
expert_anchors.self_correction: Ability to abandon or restrict a repair when evidence shows no gain or a new cost.
expert_anchors.cross_perspective_uptake: Use of a non-dominant model's failure mechanism, benchmark regime, or repair in subsequent tests.
expert_anchors.novelty_utility: Transferability of the resulting diagnostic and repair strategy to real scientific optimization.
expert_anchors.artifact_reproducibility: Frozen functions, budgets, seeds, code, environment, and complete per-run results.
